header: Test vectors for HPKE (RFC 9180) Open of a message sequence in base mode
using the ML-KEM-768 KEM from draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05. HPKE Open is
stateful and ordered: the recipient runs SetupBaseR once, then opens
each message in turn with AEAD nonce base_nonce XOR
I2OSP(sequenceNumber, Nn). Each case carries one enc and an ordered list
of decryptions to open against a single context, each with its own
result; the case result is valid, meaning the context must behave
exactly as listed. The cases cover in-order opening, out-of-order and
replayed ciphertexts, retry after a failed Open (which does not advance
the sequence number), and a 257-message sequence that reaches sequence
number 256, the first sequence number whose XOR into the nonce changes
more than the last byte. See doc/hpke.md.

LongSequence.description: 257 messages (empty aad, 3-byte plaintext) opened in order, so the last Open is at sequence number 256. ComputeNonce XORs I2OSP(seq, Nn), the full Nn-byte big-endian encoding, into base_nonce (RFC 9180 Section 5.2); at 256 the change moves from the last nonce byte to the one before it. An implementation that XORs only the low byte of the sequence number into the nonce, or keeps the counter in an 8-bit integer, computes base_nonce again at 256 and fails only the last Open. Shorter sequences cannot detect this. A 16-bit counter is not caught (that needs 65537 messages).
LongSequence.effect: The same nonce logic on the sender side reuses message 0's AEAD nonce for message 256 under the same key, which breaks the confidentiality and integrity of AES-GCM and ChaCha20Poly1305.

MultiMessage.description: A sequence of messages opened in order on one HPKE context. Each successful Open advances the sequence number, so the AEAD nonce is base_nonce XOR I2OSP(sequenceNumber, Nn); opening the messages in order MUST recover each plaintext.

OutOfOrderCiphertext.description: A ciphertext sealed at sequence number k is opened when the context is at a different sequence number j < k (a later message arrives early, as when a message is lost). The AEAD nonce base_nonce XOR I2OSP(j, Nn) differs from the one used to seal, so Open MUST fail at the tag check (RFC 9180 Section 9.7.1: ciphertexts MUST be presented to ContextR.Open() in the order they were sealed).

ReplayedCiphertext.description: A ciphertext already opened at its sequence number is replayed at a later sequence number; the nonce differs, so Open MUST fail. HPKE contexts do not accept a message twice.

RetryAfterFailedOpen.description: A failed Open is followed by further Opens on the same context. RFC 9180 Section 5.2's ContextR.Open raises OpenError before IncrementSeq, so a failed Open leaves the sequence number unchanged and the next Open uses the same nonce. The cases cover: a forged ciphertext (one tag bit flipped) followed by the genuine one; a later message's ciphertext presented at sequence 0, before any successful Open, followed by the first and second messages; and a genuine ciphertext presented with the wrong aad, followed by the same ciphertext bytes with the correct aad. Bouncy Castle Java releases r1rv81 through r1rv85 advanced the sequence number when computing the nonce, before the tag check, so every Open after a failure used the wrong nonce; fixed in r1rv85v2 (commit fa678fa7) and r1rv86 (commit 56bbae1). Some implementations instead deliberately discard the context after any failed Open. That departs from the Section 5.2 pseudocode but fails closed, in the spirit of Section 9.7.1 ("When an unrecoverable loss is detected, the application MUST discard any associated HPKE context."); such implementations reject the entries after the failure and may skip cases with this flag.
RetryAfterFailedOpen.effect: An implementation that advances the sequence number on a failed Open lets a single forged ciphertext permanently desynchronize the recipient's context from the sender: every later genuine message fails to open, a remote denial of service that needs no key material.

tests.comment: valid sequence of four messages opened in order
out-of-order: first message opened, then the third message's ciphertext opened at sequence 1
replay: first message opened again at sequence 1
retry after failed Open: forged second message rejected, then the genuine second and third messages open at sequences 1 and 2
retry at sequence 0: second message's ciphertext rejected as the first Open, then the first and second messages open at sequences 0 and 1
retry after failed Open: genuine second message presented with the wrong aad and rejected, then the same ciphertext with the correct aad opens at sequence 1 and the third message at sequence 2
valid sequence of 257 messages opened in order (sequence numbers 0 to 256)
